title: The Quiet L
kidRule: L often stays quiet when it sits between a vowel and K, F, or M, as in YOLK, CALF, and CALM. But not always: we do hear it in MILK and ELF!
hint: A quiet letter is hiding in this word. We do not say it out loud, and it sits just before the K, F, or M. Which one?
reminder: A quiet L hides just before the K, F, or M.

check.question: Why can't we hear the L in CALM?
check.correctAnswer: L often stays quiet when it sits between a vowel and K, F, or M!
distractors: Because L is always quiet in short words
Because the C uses up all the sound

words.def: Quiet and peaceful, not worried or wild.
words.sent: The lake was calm and smooth like glass.
words.story: Taking slow, deep breaths tells your heart to slow down, which helps your whole body relax!
words.card: The *cal*ico cat stayed *calm* while the jelly wobbled off the plate!

words.def: The yellow middle part of an egg.
words.sent: I dipped my toast in the runny yolk.
words.story: The color of this part of an egg depends on what the hen has been eating!
words.card: '*Yo*!' said the *yolk*, sliding off the toast on a tiny skateboard!

words.sent: The calf drank milk from its mother.
words.story: A baby elephant and a baby whale are also called by this name!
words.card: The *calf* wore a *ca*pe and mooed, 'Super Cow to the rescue!'

words.def: The long stem of a plant.
words.sent: The ladybug climbed up the corn stalk.
words.story: A corn plant can grow taller than a grown-up in just one summer!
words.card: The corn *stalk* loves to *talk* about popcorn all day long!

words.def: People, especially the ordinary people of one place.
words.sent: The friendly folk in the village waved hello.
words.story: Folk tales like Cinderella were told out loud for hundreds of years before anyone wrote them down!
words.card: The *fo*rest *folk* held a dance party for the fireflies!

words.sent: The talkative parrot said hello to everyone.
words.story: Some parrots are very talkative. A famous gray parrot named Alex learned to say more than 100 words!
words.card: My *talkative* toaster loves to *talk* about bread all morning!

words.def: The flat inside part of your hand.
words.sent: The ladybug sat in the palm of my hand.
words.story: No hair ever grows on this part of your hand!
words.card: My *pal* drew a smiley face on the *palm* of my hand!

words.def: A word for doing something in place of another person, to help them or to speak for them.
words.sent: I thanked the firefighters on behalf of our class.
words.story: Long ago, 'half' could also mean 'side'. So doing something on a friend's behalf was like standing by their side!
words.card: On *behalf* of the mice, I will take *half* of that cheese!

words.def: A big silver fish with pink meat that swims up rivers.
words.sent: The bear caught a salmon in the river.
words.story: These fish swim all the way back to the very stream where they hatched, and they find it by smell!
words.card: The *salmon* put a tiny hat *on* and leaped over the waterfall!

words.def: A sweet, oval nut with a light brown skin.
words.sent: She sprinkled a chopped almond over her oatmeal.
words.story: Almond trees are close cousins of peach trees. The part we eat is the seed from inside a fuzzy green fruit!
words.card: The *mon*key hid one *almond* in each of his cheeks!
